summary.intent: Review and close out a deadline-sensitive todo: audit all GitHub Actions in the cipher-box repo for Node 24 runtime compatibility before the June 2026 deadline.
summary.outcome: Confirmed all 16 GitHub Actions are already node24-native or composite (unaffected by the runtime migration); deadline passed without breakage. Todo moved to completed on a new branch.

repo: All 16 GitHub Actions in the repo are already node24-compatible: 11 declare `runs.using: node24` natively, 5 are composite actions unaffected by the runtime migration. No FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24 workaround was ever needed.
Repo convention: completed todos are committed inside feature PRs, never as standalone commits directly to main. Direct commits to main are blocked by a repo rule.
Actions use floating major tags (v4, v5, v6, etc.) rather than pinned SHAs — these tags already resolve to the latest stable within each major, so the fleet was self-updating.
CI on main was green post-deadline (Release Please, Codecov, E2E all passing), which was early confirmation the migration hadn't broken anything before the full audit ran.

The todo flagged 5 specific actions (tauri-apps/tauri-action, ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres, release-please-action, scp-action, ssh-action); all had been addressed before the todo was tackled — tauri became node24-native at v0.6.2, the others are composite.

code.finding: Todo written in March 2026 flagging 5 actions; by June 16 all were resolved. File was annotated with audit results and moved to .planning/todos/completed/.

workflow: Parallel agent fan-out (16 researchers, one per action) audited the entire action fleet in ~60 seconds and 344k tokens — significantly faster than sequential investigation.

Checking CI health on the target branch before starting an overdue audit is a useful shortcut: green CI means the deadline passed safely, narrowing the work to documentation/closure rather than urgent fixes.
The `--lsit` typo was silently corrected to `--list` by the routing layer — fuzzy flag matching prevents user friction on minor typos.

friction: The todo's June 2 deadline had already passed by 14 days when it was tackled; no process caught the overdue state proactively (the list display did add a warning, but only inline).
Command typo `--lsit` instead of `--list` — minor, but indicates the command name is easy to mistype.
open_items: Branch with the todo-completion commit has not been PR'd or merged; needs a PR (or squash into the next feature branch) to land on main.

9 other todos remain pending, including 3 with active deadlines or recent security findings: #6 (encrypt share itemName at rest), #7 (IPNS signature storage review S1–S3), and #8 (pin GitHub Actions to immutable SHAs — ironically, the audit confirmed floating major tags are used, not pinned SHAs).

#8 (pin GitHub Actions to immutable SHAs for supply-chain hardening) was not addressed by this session — the Node 24 audit confirmed versions are current but the actions are still on floating major tags, not pinned commit SHAs.
